item.title: #3591894: Error message for empty value is displayed for select props even when they're not required
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591894 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, choosing "- None -" on an optional select prop (one backed by an enum) no longer shows a validation error such as "data must be string". Required selects are still validated as before.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix landed in getCurrentValueFromProps() in ui/src/components/form/react-hook-form/utils/index.ts, not in shouldSkipPropValidation() as the issue body proposed. When a select had options but none was marked selected, the function returned undefined. The existing check in shouldSkipPropValidation() (componentFieldValidation.ts) only skips validation for an optional SELECT or OPTION when the value is '_none', which matches core's behavior. So the undefined value reached schema validation and failed. getCurrentValueFromProps() now returns the selected option's value if there is one. Otherwise, if props.options exists, it returns '_none', so the existing skip logic applies. The change adds Vitest unit tests in ui/tests/vitest/unit/formUtils.test.js.

item.title: #3591848: ∅ is added for empty fields, forcing translation and rendering on the page
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591848 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

When translating Canvas Pages with TMGMT, empty component inputs no longer show a literal ∅ in the review form or force the translator to fill them in. An input that is empty in the source now reads "This field is empty in the source language." An optional input can be left blank in the translation and is saved as empty. A required input still gives TMGMT's "The field is empty." error. If a translator plugin returns an exact ∅, it is discarded and the value from the default translation is kept. This fixes content translation only. Config translation jobs (ContentTemplate, PageRegion) still show, force and store ∅. Falling back to the source value at render time is not part of this change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ComponentInputsTranslatablesExtractor::EMPTY_SENTINEL (∅) is still the extracted #text for empty optional inputs, because TMGMT's Data::flatten() strips empty strings. It is now an internal marker only. TmgmtHooks implements hook_tmgmt_data_item_text_output_alter to blank it in both review columns, but only for content job items whose entity has a Canvas field. It also implements hook_form_tmgmt_job_item_edit_form_alter and hook_form_tmgmt_local_task_item_edit_form_alter. These replace the missing source textarea with a message. They also add validate callbacks that temporarily set the sentinel on empty translations of optional props, so TMGMT's "The field is empty." check passes, and restore the empty value afterwards. Required props, checked via prop_field_definitions[...]['required'] of the component version the tree item uses, are not masked and keep the error. The "Validate" and "Save as completed" buttons are handled the same way. The local task form (tmgmt_local) gets a parallel set of mask and unmask callbacks.

In ComponentTreeFieldProcessor, writeNestedTranslationsToInputs() returns NULL for a translation that is exactly the sentinel. An empty string is kept as a valid, explicitly empty translation. If every translatable leaf of a composite input (such as text_format) is NULL, the whole composite becomes NULL. setTranslations() then refills NULL values at any depth from the default translation via refillDiscardedFromDefault() and defaultTranslationInputs(). Values that stay NULL are dropped. Only an exact match is discarded, so a translation that merely contains ∅ is stored as written.

ComponentInputsTranslatablesExtractor also gets getUnresolvedSchemaDefinition(). It reads the config schema before type resolution, because core rewrites definitions in place and removes type. Without it, text_format inputs could lose their #format. A @todo points to work item 3592014 for extending the sentinel handling to config job items.

item.title: #3592084: Canvas entity edit/delete/translation routes render in the front-end theme instead of the admin theme
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592084 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The delete page (/page/{id}/delete) and the translations overview page (/page/{id}/translations) for Canvas pages used to render in the site's front-end theme. They showed the public header and navigation, and the content was unstyled. They now render in the configured admin theme. The Canvas editor itself is unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Drupal\canvas\Entity\Routing\CanvasHtmlRouteProvider extended core's DefaultHtmlRouteProvider, which never sets the _admin_route route option, so the theme negotiator fell back to the default theme. It now extends AdminHtmlRouteProvider, which sets _admin_route: TRUE on the add, edit and delete form routes it generates. content_translation copies that option from entity.canvas_page.edit_form onto entity.canvas_page.content_translation_overview, so that route is fixed too. The editor route canvas.boot.entity is defined separately in canvas.routing.yml and does not use this provider. Currently only canvas_page uses CanvasHtmlRouteProvider. The issue lists test coverage as a remaining task, and I did not check whether tests landed.

item.title: #3591930: Apply brand kit colour changes optimistically
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591930 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Editing or adding a brand kit colour in the Canvas editor now updates the swatch right away instead of waiting for the server. The form closes on save, and the editor reverts the change if the server rejects it. The colour change also reaches the page preview while the editor stays open, which didn't happen before. This also fixes colour edits not showing when a brand kit auto-save draft existed, for example after a font edit.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The changes are all in the ui/ React app. In ui/src/services/brandKit.ts, updateColor and createColor now patch the getBrandKit cache entry in onQueryStarted through a patchColors() helper, and call patchResult.undo() if the request fails. Each patch mutates a single colour in place, so undoing it cannot revert an edit to a different colour. updateColor also records a Symbol token per colour id in latestColorWrites. It rolls back only if its token is still the newest for that id, so a slow failing request cannot overwrite a later edit. createColor inserts a temporary row with a pending-<uuid> id and swaps in the server's row when the response arrives. It does not mint the final UUID on the client, which the issue body proposed. The invalidated tag changed from the literal 'global' to BRAND_KIT_ID.

useBrandKitColors now reads colours only from the canonical getBrandKit entry and no longer prefers the auto-save draft. The hook uses data instead of currentData, so optimistic patches stay visible during the refetch triggered by invalidation. The local colors state and setColors are removed. BrandKit.colors becomes optional in the type.

ColorFormPopover dispatches the mutation, then closes the popover. On failure it reopens through reopenOnFailure(), keeping the entered values and the error. For the preview, Viewport builds CSS custom properties from the live brand kit with buildColorStyles. It passes them to IframeSwapper as a new required headStyles prop. IframeSwapper injects them as a <style id="canvas-preview-head-styles"> block at the end of <head>. It updates already-loaded iframes in place and re-applies the block when a new preview iframe finishes loading.

item.title: #3592052: Site template installation fails with Canvas 1.11
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592052 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Installing a Drupal CMS site template (drush si recipes/drupal_cms_starter) failed with Canvas 1.11.0, with the error "You have requested a synthetic service ("kernel"). The DIC does not know how to construct this service." The reporter found that downgrading to Canvas 1.10.1 made the install work again. The issue is marked fixed. A related fix to the site template install path is in Canvas 1.12.0, but the issue thread does not confirm that it is the fix for this report.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The issue has no comments and no linked merge request, so the cause and fix are not stated there. I inferred a likely fix from the repository. Commit 64c59639 (#3591996, first tagged in v1.12.0) changes RecipeSubscriber so that site template page variant migration runs in a new migrateSiteTemplate() handler. That handler is registered on RecipeAppliedEvent at priority PHP_INT_MIN, so it runs after all other applied subscribers. Its docblock says installing the page template component module rebuilds the container, and that running last stops later subscribers from using the invalidated container. That matches the symptom, since a rebuilt container can fail on the synthetic kernel service. No commit references #3592052 directly, so treat the link as likely, not confirmed.

Upgrade

If site template installs fail on Canvas 1.11.0, either update to Canvas 1.12.0 or later, or pin the version the reporter confirmed works: composer require drupal/canvas:1.10.1.

item.title: #3592145: canvas-page-variant.html.twig removes #main-content
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592145 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Pages rendered through a Canvas page variant now include a #main-content anchor, so the theme's "Skip to main content" link has something to jump to. Before this, the variant template replaced the whole page and the anchor was missing. This affects every site rendering through page variants, including sites upgraded from global regions.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

CanvasPageVariant::buildPageVariant() now prefixes the route's main content, which is injected at the "Page content" marker, with the placeholder <!--canvas-main-content-anchor-->. A #post_render callback, CanvasPageVariant::resolveMainContentAnchor(), runs after the whole variant has rendered. It replaces the placeholder with <a id="main-content" tabindex="-1"></a> only if the rendered HTML has no id="main-content" already, and otherwise removes it. This avoids duplicate ids when a theme page template component renders the theme's page.html.twig, which already ships the anchor. The id match is case-sensitive and bounded, so Main-Content and main-content-foo do not count as existing anchors. The class now implements TrustedCallbackInterface for the callback. renderComponentTree() still injects main content exactly as passed, so other callers such as the headless content API are unaffected. The change is covered by new kernel tests and an update to docs/page-variants.md.

Contribution

item.title: #3591874: Upgrade the Canvas UI to React Router 7
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591874 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

The Canvas module's front-end admin application (the page-building UI) has upgraded its routing library, React Router, from version 6 to version 7. The previous version had known security advisories, so this removes that exposure for sites running Canvas. As part of the upgrade, a bug in the page preview panel was also fixed: in some navigation sequences, a canceled preview page could still be shown if it reported "ready" after the editor had already navigated away and back to it; the preview now correctly waits for the current page's iframe before swapping it in.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Canvas UI's react-router/react-router-dom dependency (used by the experimental Canvas/Experience Builder module's admin app) is upgraded from v6, which had known security advisories, to v7.

Technical details

React Router 7 merges react-router-dom into the single react-router package, so every import across the Canvas UI (App.tsx, AppRoutes.tsx, CodeEditorRouteGuard.tsx, ErrorBoundary.tsx, ConflictResolutionPage.tsx, ReviewChangesPage.tsx, useEditorNavigation.ts, and the related test files) was changed from react-router-dom to react-router, and RouterProvider is now imported from react-router/dom in AppRoutes.tsx. The five v6 opt-in compatibility flags (v7_fetcherPersist, v7_normalizeFormMethod, v7_partialHydration, v7_relativeSplatPath, v7_skipActionErrorRevalidation) are removed from createBrowserRouter's future option and from MemoryRouter usages in tests, since that behavior is now the v7 default.

In HeadlessPreview.tsx, the double-buffered preview frame logic was reworked: activateFrame's ref-based check (currentFrameKeyRef) against a "newer navigation" was replaced with a pendingReady flag on PreviewFrameState, set via a new markFrameReady callback wrapped in startTransition. The promotion from pending to active now happens inside the existing route-sync useEffect (which now also depends on frames.pendingReady), so a pending iframe is only promoted if it still matches the currently committed route, preventing a canceled page from being shown if it reports readiness late. The Playwright CanvasNavigation helper's preview-wait logic was also updated to wait for visible preview content instead of a full document load, since SPA navigation no longer triggers one.

Upgrade

Developers extending or patching the Canvas UI's TypeScript/React code should update their own imports:

// before
import { useNavigate, Outlet } from 'react-router-dom';

// after
import { useNavigate, Outlet } from 'react-router';

and, for RouterProvider specifically:

import { RouterProvider } from 'react-router/dom';

react-router-dom is no longer a dependency; only react-router (^7.18.4) is required.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 24, 2026

item.title: #3592142: ColorFormPopover resets edits in progress when the color list refetches
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592142 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In Canvas's brand kit color editor, editing a color's values (e.g. dragging the RGB sliders) could silently revert to the previously saved value if the color list happened to refetch in the background while the popover was still open, such as right after a related save. Users would lose their in-progress edits with no warning. The popover's form now only initializes once per time it is opened, so a refreshed color object arriving mid-edit no longer wipes out unsaved changes.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ColorFormPopover reinitialized its form state in a useEffect keyed on [open, operation, color]. Because color is a fresh object identity after each brand kit refetch (e.g. from RTK Query cache updates), any refetch while the popover was open re-ran INIT_EDIT/INIT_ADD and overwrote whatever the user had typed.

The fix adds an initializedRef (via useRef) that is set to true the first time the effect runs after open becomes true, and reset to false when the popover closes. Subsequent re-renders with a new color reference while open stays true now skip the updateForm dispatch entirely, so the reducer state (and thus the visible form inputs) is left alone until the popover is closed and reopened. A new test, ColorFormPopover.test.tsx, verifies this by re-rendering with a new color object after a field is edited and asserting the edited value and derived preview persist.

Contribution

item.title: #3592129: CanvasOauthAuthenticationProvider does not allow OAuth authentication on the folder config entity external API route
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592129 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Sites using the canvas_oauth module together with the Canvas CLI (@drupal-canvas/cli) could not sync folders or page templates via npx canvas pull when using OAuth2 client-credentials authentication. The request to fetch folder configuration was rejected with "The used authentication method is not allowed on this route," even though the OAuth client had the correct permissions. This is now fixed: OAuth2 bearer-token authentication is accepted on the folder config entity API route, matching how it already worked for components, JavaScript components, asset libraries, brand kits, content templates, and page variants.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

CanvasOauthAuthenticationProvider::applies() gates OAuth2 authentication on Canvas's external config entity API routes using an explicit $protected_config_entity_types allowlist. Folder::ENTITY_TYPE_ID had been omitted from that list, so for requests to /canvas/api/v0/config/folder the provider's applies() returned FALSE, the simple_oauth delegation never ran, and Drupal core's AuthenticationSubscriber rejected the bearer token as not allowed on that route, even though folder is a valid HTTP-API-eligible config entity type per the canvas_config_entity_type_id route requirement.

The fix simply adds Folder::ENTITY_TYPE_ID to the allowlist alongside the existing entries. The corresponding kernel test case in CanvasOauthAuthenticationProviderTest was updated from expecting FALSE to TRUE for the folder entity type to cover this route.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3592002: Normalize agent-written prop values against their schema and report values the component source cannot store
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592002 · 1 contributor · 34 comments

Summary

Canvas's AI page builder tools (place_components, edit_components) validate and store the component prop values an LLM writes as YAML. In practice, models like GPT-5.2 often write the same value in a technically-different but equivalent textual shape, for example a percentage wrapped in an extra pair of quotes, or a number or boolean written as a quoted string. Those used to fail schema validation outright, forcing the AI agent to retry the whole component placement. Separately, when the model supplied a value a prop genuinely could not store, such as a partial image object or a bare URL for a media-backed field, that prop was silently dropped rather than rejected, so the component got placed without it and could render broken (a Twig error, or an empty props form) until the page was reloaded. This fix normalizes AI-supplied prop values against their schema before validating and storing them, and turns previously-silent dropped values into a clear validation error naming the prop, so the AI has a chance to correct its output instead of producing a broken component.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AiResponseValidator::validateComponentStructure() now returns the normalized component groups array instead of void; callers must use the returned value, not their original input, to get the prop values that were actually validated and should be stored.

Technical details

The fix adds CanvasAiPropValueNormalizer (canvas_ai.prop_value_normalizer, marked @internal), whose normalizeProps()/normalizeValue() walk each prop's JSON schema (from propSources[$prop]['jsonSchema']): it strips one matching outer quote pair before treating a value as an enum member or a URI-formatted string, casts numeric/boolean-looking strings to their typed form, and recurses into object properties and array items. Free-form string props without an enum or format hint are left untouched, so prose keeps its quotes. AiResponseValidator::convertToComponentTreeData() now runs each component's props through this normalizer before calling clientModelToInput(), and validateComponentStructure()'s signature changed from void to returning the normalized $componentGroups, so a caller that doesn't use the return value gets unnormalized data back.

A second change, collectUnstorableValueViolations(), compares the AI-supplied props against the $inputs array clientModelToInput() actually produced: any prop present in the input but missing from the output (previously silently dropped) becomes a ConstraintViolationException naming the prop, with a hint to supply a valid entity ID when the prop's sourceTypeSettings.storage.target_type points at a reference field (e.g. media).

Both changes are wired into PlaceComponents and EditComponents, which now use validateComponentStructure()'s return value (EditComponents echoes back only the normalized values for the props each edit actually changed). SetAIGeneratedComponentStructure and SetAIGeneratedTemplateData still call validateComponentStructure() but, per the diff, were not updated to capture its return value, so only two of the four AI tools mentioned in the issue pick up the normalized (rather than as-written) values downstream.

Upgrade

Code calling AiResponseValidator::validateComponentStructure() directly must now use its return value instead of relying on the input array being mutated or validated in place:

// Before:
$this->responseValidator->validateComponentStructure($operation['components']);

// After:
$operation['components'] = $this->responseValidator->validateComponentStructure($operation['components']);

item.title: #3592057: Support mapping multi-valued list fields to array-type component props
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592057 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas's automatic field-to-prop mapping now recognizes multi-valued list fields (list_string, list_integer, list_float with unlimited or multiple cardinality) as valid sources for component props that expect an array of scalars, such as {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}. Previously, even though this was a natural mapping, Canvas excluded any multi-valued field from its suggestions, so these list fields never showed up when configuring a content template's component mapping. Site builders can now select these fields in that scenario.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The exclusion lived in two places that both blanket-rejected any field with cardinality other than 1: ApiUiContentEntityReferenceControllers::listEntityFields()(ish) and MultiValuedFieldNotSupportedConstraintValidator. Both now carve out an exception via \is_a($field_definition->getItemDefinition()->getClass(), ListItemBase::class, TRUE), so multi-valued fields whose item class extends Drupal\options\Plugin\Field\FieldType\ListItemBase (i.e. the list field types) are no longer rejected outright.

On the matching side, EntityFieldPropSourceMatcher already skipped list_float and list_integer field types except for a small set of "allowed" prop schemas (type: number/integer), via the IGNORE_FIELD_TYPES constant (renamed its exceptions key to allowed for clarity). list_string could not be added there because its field item class, ListStringItem, isn't referenceable from this namespace per the phpat.shapeMatcher architecture rule, so a new IGNORE_FIELD_TYPES_BY_ID constant was added, keyed by field type ID string instead of class, currently containing only list_string restricted to {"type": "string"} props (no enum). Both constants are consulted in the field-scanning loop that builds prop match suggestions. Since array-typed props strip type: array down to their items schema and set $cardinality from maxItems before delegating to the scalar matcher, these allowed-schema checks now also apply correctly to multi-valued list fields feeding array props.

One side effect: a previously-existing match of one_from_an_string_list against type: string&$ref=…color was removed from the test fixtures, since a single-valued list_string field with a color-format constraint is no longer considered an unconditional match under the new allowed-schema rule.

item.title: #3592060: Canvas AI: Update orchestrator for content-only / page-variant chrome
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592060 · 1 contributor · 33 comments

Summary

Canvas's AI orchestrator, the agent that decides which specialized AI agent (page builder, template builder, etc.) should handle a user's request, previously still assumed that pages have theme-global header/footer/sidebar regions that its builder agents can fill in. After a related change moved that "chrome" into page variants (edited separately in the Canvas editor), the orchestrator's prompt was left describing the old model: it would tell users it could "build complete pages with headers, footers, and multiple sections" and would route a request like "add a header to this page" to the page builder agent, which no longer has any way to place chrome. This update rewrites the orchestrator's instructions so it correctly explains that headers, footers, navigation, and sidebars come from the page variant (called a "page template" in the editor), and instead of invoking a builder agent for such requests, it now points users to the specific places in the Canvas editor where the page template can be edited.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New canvas_ai_post_update_0014_reimport_orchestrator_content_only_chrome() reimports the ai_agents.ai_agent.canvas_ai_orchestrator config entity's system_prompt on update, overwriting any direct customizations of that prompt.

Technical details

The fix is entirely in the system_prompt text of config/install/ai_agents.ai_agent.canvas_ai_orchestrator.yml, plus a new post-update hook, canvas_ai_post_update_0014_reimport_orchestrator_content_only_chrome() in canvas_ai.post_update.php, that reimports just that key (preserving the config entity's uuid and _core hash) so existing sites pick up the corrected prompt.

The prompt changes: the tool blurb for canvas_template_builder_agent now says it builds "a complete page body ... in the content region" and explicitly does not build headers, footers, or sidebars. A new "Rule #9: Site Chrome Comes From the Page Variant" instructs the orchestrator to still call the template builder for a full page request that also asks for a header/footer, but with a prompt scoped to the page body only, and to not call any builder agent at all when the user asks only to add/modify a header or footer on an existing page. Instead it should explain that chrome comes from the page variant and name the three UI entry points to edit it: the "Page templates" section of the Templates panel, the outermost row of the Layers panel, and the "Edit template" link on the "Page data" tab. Several few-shot examples and anti-pattern bullets were updated to match. CanvasAiOrchestratorPostUpdateTest was extended with a data provider covering both post-updates 0003 and 0014 that reimport this prompt, asserting the new prompt text is present and the old "including headers, footers, and multiple sections" wording is gone.

This is a direct follow-up to #3592030, which made the same content-only change to the page and template builder agents themselves; this issue closes the gap by updating the orchestrator that routes to them.

item.title: #3592111: Unify headless frame-ancestors policies across frameworks
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592111 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Canvas headless frontends embed inside the Canvas editor's iframe during draft preview, which requires the frontend's Content-Security-Policy to allow that specific embedding via frame-ancestors. Each framework adapter (Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, TanStack Start) previously computed this policy on its own, and at least one combination, Vercel-hosted Next.js apps, ended up refusing the embed entirely, blocking preview and editing of the headless site from within Canvas. All adapters now share one resolver for this policy, so the behavior is consistent and documented across frameworks, and site owners get an explicit CANVAS_EDITOR_ORIGINS setting to override the defaults when needed.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New CANVAS_EDITOR_ORIGINS environment variable (a whitespace- or comma-separated list of origins) that explicitly sets which origins may embed a headless frontend for draft preview. When unset, the policy defaults to 'self' plus the CANVAS_SITE_URL origin and the current draft session's editor origin; setting CANVAS_EDITOR_ORIGINS (even to an empty or fully invalid value) replaces both defaults rather than adding to them.

Technical details

The policy logic now lives in one place, resolveFrameAncestors() and mergeFrameAncestors() in packages/headless/src/server/csp.ts, exported from @drupal-canvas/headless/server, and every adapter's middleware/plugin (headless-next's applyCanvasHeaders(), headless-nuxt's beforeResponse server plugin, headless-astro's onRequest middleware, headless-tanstack-start's cspMiddleware) calls the same two functions instead of building the header itself.

resolveFrameAncestors() reads process.env.CANVAS_EDITOR_ORIGINS on every call. When set, it replaces both defaults with the parsed list (split on whitespace or commas); when unset, it falls back to CANVAS_SITE_URL plus the current draft session's renewUrl origin. Every candidate goes through toEditorOrigin(), which normalizes to scheme, host, and port and rejects anything that is not a plain http(s) URL: credentialed URLs, wildcard or CSP-delimiter-bearing hosts, and literal IPv6 addresses are all dropped (DNS hostnames that resolve to IPv6 still work). 'self' is always included, and origins are deduplicated.

mergeFrameAncestors() folds the resolved directive into whatever Content-Security-Policy value(s) the app already set, handling repeated header fields, array values, and comma-separated policy lists uniformly, and leaves an application-owned frame-ancestors directive untouched rather than overriding it. This is embedding policy only; it does not affect draft authentication or postMessage trust between the editor and the frontend. The Astro and TanStack Start Vite integrations also now load CANVAS_EDITOR_ORIGINS from framework .env files into process.env, matching how they already load CANVAS_SITE_URL.

Upgrade

Optional. To explicitly control which origins may embed the frontend for draft preview, set the new variable in the frontend's environment, for example:

CANVAS_EDITOR_ORIGINS=https://cms.example, https://staging.example:8443

Leave it unset to keep the default behavior ('self' plus CANVAS_SITE_URL and the draft session's editor origin). Setting it to an empty string suppresses both defaults and admits only 'self'.

item.title: #3592125: Preserve local package.json when pulling code components
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592125 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The Canvas CLI's canvas pull command used to overwrite a project's local package.json entirely with the version stored in Drupal, discarding any custom scripts, dependencies, or metadata the developer had added locally. Now, when a local package.json already exists, pull preserves it and only adds dependencies from the pulled manifest that are missing locally, leaving existing versions, scripts, and other fields untouched. If no local file exists, the pulled manifest is still written as before, and --skip-overwrite continues to leave an existing file alone entirely.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix replaces the previous overwrite-or-skip logic in createAssetsPullTask (packages/cli/src/commands/pull.ts) with a merge step implemented in the new mergePackageJsonDependencies utility (packages/cli/src/utils/merge-package-json.ts). It compares the pulled dependencies against the local file's dependencies, devDependencies, and peerDependencies: any pulled dependency whose name already appears in any of those three sections is left alone (add-only, no version bumps), and anything missing is inserted into local dependencies using the pulled version spec. All other local fields (name, version, scripts, custom sections like overrides) are copied through unchanged, and the file is rewritten with 2-space indentation only when at least one dependency was actually added; otherwise the on-disk file is left byte-identical.

Each added dependency is now reported as its own Dependency result item (itemType: 'Dependency', detail 'Added'), and the "run npm install" reminder note only fires when something changed, either a fresh file write or an added dependency. If the local package.json is invalid JSON, the merge throws and the command reports Could not merge dependencies: ... for that item while leaving the local file untouched and letting the rest of the pull continue.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3592099: Add headless previews for entities
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592099 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Sites using Canvas Headless previously showed an empty page when a published node, page, or other Canvas-managed entity was opened directly on the Drupal domain, since Drupal has no theme to render the frontend-owned component tree. This release embeds the configured headless frontend in those pages instead: authenticated users with the preview permission now see the actual frontend rendering inside an iframe, with Drupal's toolbar, admin navigation, and status messages still visible around it. Links that resolve to Drupal-owned destinations navigate normally in the parent window, while frontend-only links stay inside the iframe. The same embedding now also covers node form previews, revision routes, and Content Moderation's "latest version" routes, letting editors preview unsaved drafts and past revisions through the real frontend rather than through Drupal's own rendering. A new excludeAutoSave option lets a preview request render only saved content, ignoring in-progress Canvas auto-saves.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\canvas_headless\Routing\CanvasContentRoute::resolve() identifies the entity and view mode shared by Drupal and frontend rendering for canonical, preview, revision, and latest_version routes; new EmbeddedPreviewSubscriber selects a canvas_headless_preview page display variant to embed the frontend.

Technical details

The core addition is Drupal\canvas_headless\EventSubscriber\EmbeddedPreviewSubscriber, which hooks RenderEvents::SELECT_PAGE_DISPLAY_VARIANT at priority -110 (after Canvas's own -100 variant selection) and, for eligible authenticated requests, swaps in the new EmbeddedHeadlessPreviewPageVariant display variant. That variant renders an iframe pointed at the frontend's preview URL plus Drupal's status messages, and ships a new headless.preview library (built from the new @drupal-canvas/headless-embedded-preview package) that handles session bootstrap and link navigation delegation via the existing @drupal-canvas/headless-host package.

Route identification is centralized in the new Drupal\canvas_headless\Routing\CanvasContentRoute value object, replacing the old CanvasContentRouteEnhancer::PRIMARY_ENTITY_PARAMETER mechanism. It recognizes entity.*.canonical, .preview, .revision, and .latest_version route names, resolves the correct entity and view mode, and flags whether the route is a "preview" (unsaved form values or a specific revision) versus a normal canonical view. CanvasContentController and CanvasEntityController use this to decide $use_auto_save independently from $is_entity_preview, since preview/revision routes must render the exact selected content (never a Canvas auto-save) and must disable render and response caching (max-age = 0), matching core's NodePreviewController behavior. A new NodePreviewAccessCheck decorates core's access_check.node.preview to grant read-only access to a preview token's subject without also granting the write access core normally requires for node previews.

CanvasContentEntityRenderer::containsThemePageTemplate() was inverted into public isHeadlessCompatiblePageVariant(), reused by both the controller and the new subscriber to decide whether a page variant can be embedded. On the frontend SDK side, fetchPage() in @drupal-canvas/headless, -next, -nuxt, -astro, -angular, and -tanstack-start now reads preview context per request (via a new preview-context.ts module and excludeAutoSave support) instead of a shared draft session, so multiple open tabs no longer clobber each other's rendering settings, and a new navigation-bridge.ts in @drupal-canvas/headless delegates eligible embedded link clicks to the host Drupal window in draft mode.

item.title: #3592101: Make React Code Components portable across Drupal and headless frontends
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592101 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

React Code Components (the small React components authors write for Canvas) previously had to use Drupal-specific APIs to read page metadata, site branding, and content, which meant they could not be reused as-is in a headless frontend. This change makes the same component code work unmodified in both Drupal-rendered pages and React-based headless applications (Next.js, TanStack Start, Astro). Existing components keep working in Drupal and in Canvas Workbench previews without any changes; the canvas pull CLI command can also automatically rewrite eligible components to the new APIs when the connected site and installed package support it. Headless applications also gain a same-origin JSON:API proxy so browser-side requests (including draft/preview reads) can reach Drupal safely without exposing credentials.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: getPageData(), getSiteData(), new JsonApiClient(), Region, and RegionsProvider are deprecated; they keep working in Drupal-rendered Code Components and Workbench but throw actionable migration errors in headless React apps.
  • New API: New drupal-canvas/react exports usePageContext(), useSiteContext(), CanvasContextProvider, useJsonApiClient(), and JsonApiClientProvider give React Code Components a single, framework-portable way to read page/site data and make JSON:API requests.

Technical details

The core addition is a shared CanvasContext ({ page, site }) carried by a new CanvasContextProvider (packages/drupal-canvas/src/context.tsx) and read with usePageContext()/useSiteContext(). Rendering integrations, the Drupal island renderer, the headless CanvasComponentTree, and both Workbench preview paths, mount the provider automatically; a missing provider or missing page/site value makes the hooks return null and emit a deduplicated warnOnce() warning rather than fetching data or defaulting. Headless SDK's fetchPage() now returns this context alongside the component tree as page.context.

JSON:API access is consolidated the same way: useJsonApiClient()/JsonApiClientProvider (packages/drupal-canvas/src/jsonapi-client-context.tsx) expose a shared JsonApiClient built on @drupal-api-client/json-api-client (createJsonApiClient() in jsonapi-client.ts), replacing separate client implementations previously used by the drupal-canvas package and the headless SDK's draft client. Browser requests in headless apps go through a new same-origin proxy (packages/headless/src/server/jsonapi-proxy.ts, and jsonapi-proxy.ts/jsonapi-proxy.test.ts in drupal-canvas) that authenticates from the draft-preview session cookie, restricts requests to the configured backend and endpoint set, and keeps authenticated responses out of shared caches.

Legacy API compatibility is enforced with an explicit runtime marker rather than environment sniffing: declareCanvasRuntime()/getCanvasRuntime() (packages/drupal-canvas/src/runtime.ts) is set by Drupal and Workbench integrations, and assertLegacyRuntime() (migration.ts) throws an actionable error, including an AI-agent migration prompt, when getPageData(), getSiteData(), or new JsonApiClient() is invoked outside those two environments. On the PHP side, CanvasContentContextBuilder and changes to CodeComponentDataProvider and SiteDataController supply this context data and advertise capabilities.contextHooks from /canvas/api/v0/site-data, which the CLI's pull codemod (packages/cli/src/utils/getter-codemod.ts, context-hook-support.ts) checks before rewriting a component's safe, unconditional getPageData()/getSiteData() calls to the new hooks. Region and RegionsProvider are deprecated in favor of the page-variants model from ADR 19.

Upgrade

No action is required to keep existing Code Components working in Drupal or Workbench. To make a component portable to headless frontends, migrate off the deprecated APIs:

// Before
import { getPageData, getSiteData } from 'drupal-canvas';

// After
import { usePageContext, useSiteContext } from 'drupal-canvas/react';

export default function PageHeader() {
  const page = usePageContext();
  const site = useSiteContext();
  if (!page || !site) return null;
  return (
    <header>
      <a href={site.branding.homeUrl}>{site.branding.siteName}</a>
      <h1>{page.pageTitle}</h1>
    </header>
  );
}

Replace direct client construction the same way:

// Before
const client = new JsonApiClient({ baseUrl });

// After
import { useJsonApiClient } from 'drupal-canvas/react';
const client = useJsonApiClient();

Running canvas pull against a site that advertises capabilities.contextHooks (and with drupal-canvas/react installed) converts eligible files automatically and reports any calls it could not safely convert.

item.title: #3592097: Include language alternates in Headless content API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592097 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Headless frontends built on Canvas can now get everything needed for a language switcher directly from the content API response, instead of having to derive it themselves. Each fetchPage() response's route object now lists every enabled language with its localized name, native name, a URL, whether that translation actually exists and is viewable, and whether it is the one currently being served. This mirrors the translation data already exposed to Code Components via getPageData(), so both APIs behave consistently.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: route in the Headless content API response now includes negotiatedLanguage and a translations list (langcode, name, nativeName, url, translationAvailable, current, external) for every enabled language.

Technical details

The new Drupal\canvas_headless\CanvasContentTranslationLinks service builds this data in CanvasContentController, and delegates the actual per-language enumeration to a new shared helper, Drupal\canvas\EntityTranslationMetadata::build(). That helper was extracted from the existing logic in CodeComponentDataProvider (which now calls it too), so Code Components and the headless API share one source of truth for langcode, name, nativeName, translationAvailable, and current. translationAvailable reflects both existence and view access; a denied or missing translation reports false and falls back to the entity's own URL in that language.

For the headless case, URL generation is more involved than the Code Component fallback: CanvasContentTranslationLinks::switchLinks() walks enabled language negotiation methods in configured order (following LanguageNegotiationUI delegation to the interface-language session negotiator), builds each link via the module's LanguageSwitcherInterface plugins, and strips out Canvas's editor-preview query parameters while forcing the session query parameter when session negotiation is active, so a translation link is unambiguous regardless of prior session state. Generated absolute URLs are then normalized by the new Drupal\canvas_headless\CanvasContentUrl::normalize(), which strips the scheme, host, and Drupal base path from same-site URLs (an external one is left absolute and flagged with external: true) so frontends can safely feed the result back into fetchPage(). The near-identical logic previously duplicated in CanvasContentResponseSubscriber for redirect targets was consolidated into this same helper.

The OpenAPI schema (RouteTranslation) and the SDK's TypeScript types (DrupalRouteTranslation, DrupalRoute in packages/headless/src/page.ts) were updated to document the new required negotiatedLanguage and translations fields, and docs/multilingual-sites-with-canvas-headless.md explains the filtering and public-URL-mapping pattern for consumers building a switcher.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">No breaking changes to existing fields. Frontends consuming fetchPage() and using the SDK's TypeScript types should update to a version that includes negotiatedLanguage and translations on DrupalRoute, since these are now required properties of the response schema. To build a switcher of only viewable translations:

const page = await fetchPage("/fr/page/1");
if (page && !("redirect" in page)) {
  const languageLinks = page.route.translations
    .filter((translation) => translation.translationAvailable)
    .map((translation) => ({
      label: translation.nativeName,
      active: translation.current,
      href: toPublicUrl(translation.langcode, translation.url),
    }));
}

Entries with external: true are absolute URLs (e.g. from domain-based language negotiation) and are not valid fetchPage() input; map them to a public URL instead of passing them back in.</parameter> <parameter name="collaboration">

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)

Summary

Drupal Canvas's headless frontend tooling now supports Angular. A new @drupal-canvas/headless-angular adapter package and an experimental Angular starter template join the existing Next.js, Astro, Nuxt and TanStack Start integrations offered through Canvas Create. Developers can now build headless Angular 21 or 22 apps that render Canvas's component trees with server-side rendering and hydration, named slots, component discovery, and full support for Canvas's draft preview and publishing workflow. The starter defaults to Angular 22 and documents Angular 21 setup; Angular Workbench integration is explicitly out of scope for now.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New @drupal-canvas/headless-angular package providing Angular 21/22 bindings (component-tree rendering, SSR/hydration, draft-preview server endpoints, and a canvas-angular codegen tool) for building headless Canvas frontends, plus a new experimental angular starter template in Canvas Create.

Technical details

The new @drupal-canvas/headless-angular package mirrors the structure of the other framework adapters and builds on the shared, framework-agnostic @drupal-canvas/headless core (its client, server, components-endpoint, and component-registry submodules). It exposes:

  • Rendering primitives (CanvasComponentTree, CanvasElement, CanvasSlot, CanvasChildren, CanvasMarkerDirective, CanvasMarkup) built on Angular signals and NgComponentOutlet, which walk the component tree, resolve named slots against a CanvasComponentRegistry, and emit the data-canvas-* marker templates used by the visual editor.
  • An application layer (CanvasPageStore, canvasPageResolver, CanvasDraftSession, CanvasDocumentHead, provideCanvas()) that wires page data into Angular's router (via a resolver and TransferState for hydration), manages the draft-session/renewal state machine, and syncs <head> metadata.
  • A server layer (createCanvasHandler, createCanvasRequest in @drupal-canvas/headless-angular/server) implementing the same REST-style endpoints as the other adapters (/api/draft, /api/draft/renew, /api/disable-draft, /api/canvas/components, /api/canvas/page, /api/canvas/entity), enforcing private/no-store caching, CSP frame-ancestors merging for embedded previews, and an explicit allowlist (CanvasSession) so tokens and PKCE verifiers never cross into the browser-visible TransferState.
  • A canvas-angular CLI/tooling script that generates a browser-safe component registry module and a server-only metadata manifest module, meant to run before ng serve/ng build, analogous to the codegen used by the other adapters.

The package targets Angular's partial compilation output (verified by a build test asserting ɵɵngDeclareComponent rather than ɵɵdefineComponent in the built bundle) so it can be consumed by both Angular 21 (TypeScript 5.9) and Angular 22 (TypeScript 6) host apps via matching peer dependency ranges.

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592030 · 1 contributor · 56 comments

Summary

Canvas moved from theme-global regions (header, footer, sidebar, etc.) to page variants, where everything besides a page's main content is built as its own component tree in the Canvas editor. The Canvas AI module still had leftover instructions and an admin settings page from the old multi-region model, describing a capability that no longer exists. This change removes them: the AI page builder and template builder agents no longer reference regions other than content, and the "Page Variant Descriptions" admin settings page (where an admin could describe how AI should treat each page variant) is deleted since nothing read those descriptions anymore. Site owners who had configured page variant descriptions for AI will find that settings page and its data gone; AI-generated pages and templates will only ever place components in the content region, with header, navigation, footer or sidebar sections generated inside that same region only when explicitly requested in the prompt.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The canvas_ai.page_variant.settings config object and its admin form at /admin/config/ai/canvas-ai-page-variant-settings ("Page Variant Descriptions") are removed; update hooks delete any existing config and rebuild routes.

The [canvas_ai:available_regions] token is deleted from CanvasAiHooks::canvas_ai_token_info()/canvas_ai_tokens(), along with CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper::getAvailableRegions() and its helpers resolveVariantForContext()/getVariantDescription(), which used to resolve a page variant via PageVariantResolver and pull a per-variant AI description out of canvas_ai.page_variant.settings. Both CanvasBuilder and CanvasDevAiBuilder controllers drop the available_regions token context accordingly.

The canvas_page_builder_agent and canvas_template_builder_agent system prompts (ai_agents.ai_agent.*.yml) are rewritten to state that content is the only region components can be placed in; canvas_template_builder_agent's description and prompt no longer mention adapting to theme-specific region names, and its YAML output format uses a fixed content key instead of region_name. Per the issue's stated scope, the region parameter accepted by the placement tools (PlaceComponents, PlacementOperation, etc.) and validated via CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper::getRegionIndex()/validateRegionExists() is left untouched, deferred to a follow-up issue.
